met_analysis:
The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal off Andhra Pradesh coast moved slowly northwestwards, crossed Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam to the Southwest of Yanam near latitude 16.450N and 81.90E, about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40 km southwest of Yanam and 60 km southwest of Kakinada during 0200 - 0800 hours IST of today, the 28th October, 2026 as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph. Latest observations indicate that the landfall process completed with the central region moving completely into land by 0800 hrs IST. Continuing to move further northwestwards, it lies centered at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 28th October, 2026 over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, near latitude 16.5°N and longitude 81.9°E, about 20 km east-nortrheast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 40 km southwest of Yanam (Puducherry UT), 60 km southwest of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 90 km east-northeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 120 km east of Gannavaram (Andhra Pradesh) and 120 km southwest of Tuni. It is very likely to move north-northwestwards during next 48 hours and weaken gradually. It will weaken into a Cyclonic Storm during next 06 hours and further into a Deep Depression during subsequent 06 hours.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood extending upto 5.8 km above mean sea level persists. Under its influence, a low pressure are is likely to form over the same region during next 24 hours.
The cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood persists at1.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance now seen as a cyclonic circulation over Jammu and neighbourhood between 3.1 and 4.5 km above mean sea level.
A fresh Western Disturbance seen as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 67°E to the north of Lat. 28°N.
The trough from Westcentral Bay of Bengal close to Andhra Pradesh coast to cyclonic circulation associated with the very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal off Andhra Pradesh coast upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Uttar Pradesh & adjoining Bihar at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
